defect.evidence_quote: First, the warrantless arrest was lawful — a warrantless felony arrest in public on probable cause does not violate the Fourth Amendment — so the consent was not the product of an illegal arrest.
defect.locator_note: ^rule-arrest-warrant; Watson 423-24 and Devenpeck 153 in the callout
defect.problem: The black-letter callout cannot be fully verified as framed. The disclosed Watson record supports a warrantless public felony arrest on probable cause, but not the added breadth that the rule applies even when there was time to get a warrant or the 423-24 pincite. The disclosed Devenpeck record supports objective/offense-agnostic probable cause, but not the separate subjective-motive formulation as cited.
defect.proposed_fix: Either add verified Watson opinion text/pinpoints for the time-to-warrant proposition and cite Whren or al-Kidd for subjective motive, or narrow the rule to the disclosed support: warrantless public arrest on probable cause; Atwater for minor fine-only offenses; Devenpeck for objective/offense-agnostic probable cause; Payton for the home threshold.

reasons: Watson pin-424 only states that a warrantless felony arrest in public on probable cause does not violate the Fourth Amendment; no disclosed Watson field or text file verifies the phrase even when there was time to get a warrant.
Atwater is supported by the lake treatment scope note for very minor fine-only misdemeanors and no case-by-case balancing.
Devenpeck pin-153 says only: No; the inquiry is objective and offense-agnostic. The disclosed Devenpeck evidence does not mention subjective motive.
Payton pin-590 supports the home-threshold qualification, but the callout cites only an internal page for that sentence.
No text directory was disclosed, and the cited Watson, Atwater, and Devenpeck lake pinpoints are not star-verified for the callout passages.
residual_risks: The unsupported subclaims may be true in the actual opinions, but they are not verifiable from the disclosed files.
Several relevant lake pinpoints show quote_fidelity mismatch or slip-only status.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Split the rule into separately cited subclaims and use only verified pins: Watson for warrantless public arrest on probable cause, Atwater for minor fine-only offenses, Devenpeck for objective/offense-agnostic probable cause, Whren or al-Kidd for motive, and Payton for the home threshold.
